{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1794683164740,"sessionID":"ses_e248c4137ffeLN9ljlyo6Pk1cw","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"bash","callID":"toolu_01UZS9BUvWgkEhuR46BcNLVr","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"command":"cd /app && ls -la && wc -l lightlag_client.py lightlag_surface.py detach.py && cat lightlag_surface.py && cat detach.py && cat lightlag_client.py"},"output":"total 24\ndrwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 14 15:03 .\ndrwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 14 18:58 ..\n-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2830 Nov 14 15:03 detach.py\n-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 3518 Nov 14 11:06 lightlag_client.py\n-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 7822 Nov 14 15:03 lightlag_surface.py\n  102 lightlag_client.py\n  152 lightlag_surface.py\n   61 detach.py\n  315 total\n\"\"\"The ground and the drive physics of the traverse, as published.\n\nEverything here is public: `rules()` gives the numbers and `map()` the grid. The simulator\nruns a drive through `drive()` with the hidden values; a controller can run the same function\nwith its own estimates, so nobody has to guess how the published formulas are applied.\nStandard library only, Python 3.9+.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple\n\nTERRAIN_CODES = {\"b\": \"bedrock\", \"r\": \"regolith\", \"s\": \"sand\", \"k\": \"rocks\"}\n\n# Published physics. `rules()` returns this table unchanged.\nPHYSICS: Dict[str, Any] = {\n    \"segment_m\": 0.25,                  # a drive is integrated in steps of this many wheel metres\n    \"max_tilt\": 0.36,                   # rise over run (about 20 degrees); steeper ground stops the rover\n    \"slip_base_ranges\": {\"bedrock\": [0.01, 0.05], \"regolith\": [0.05, 0.12],\n                         \"sand\": [0.15, 0.35], \"rocks\": [0.12, 0.24]},\n    \"slip_grade_gain\": {\"bedrock\": 0.8, \"regolith\": 1.5, \"sand\": 3.5, \"rocks\": 1.2},\n    \"slip_noise\": 0.02,                 # one uniform draw in +-this per executed drive\n    \"slip_max\": 0.95,\n    \"side_slip_gain\": {\"bedrock\": 0.1, \"regolith\": 0.3, \"sand\": 0.8, \"rocks\": 0.2},\n    \"drive_cost_per_wheel_m\": {\"bedrock\": 0.30, \"regolith\": 0.36, \"sand\": 0.50, \"rocks\": 0.60},\n    \"climb_cost_per_m\": 2.0,            # energy per metre of height gained; descending returns nothing\n}\n\n\nclass Surface:\n    \"\"\"A height grid with bilinear interpolation, and one terrain class per grid cell.\n\n    `elevation_cm[j][i]` is the height in centimetres at x = i * cell, y = j * cell.\n    `terrain[j][i]` is the class code of the cell with that vertex as its south-west corner.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, cell: float, elevation_cm: Sequence[Sequence[int]], terrain: Sequence[str]) -> None:\n        self.cell = float(cell)\n        self.h: List[List[float]] = [[value / 100.0 for value in row] for row in elevation_cm]\n        self.ny, self.nx = len(self.h), len(self.h[0])\n        if self.ny < 2 or self.nx < 2 or any(len(row) != self.nx for row in self.h):\n            raise ValueError(\"the elevation grid must be rectangular, at least 2 by 2\")\n        if len(terrain) != self.ny - 1 or any(len(row) != self.nx - 1 for row in terrain):\n            raise ValueError(\"terrain needs one code per grid cell\")\n        self.codes: List[str] = [str(row) for row in terrain]\n        self.width = (self.nx - 1) * self.cell\n        self.height = (self.ny - 1) * self.cell\n\n    def inside(self, x: float, y: float) -> bool:\n        return 0.0 <= x <= self.width and 0.0 <= y <= self.height\n\n    def locate(self, x: float, y: float) -> Tuple[int, int, float, float]:\n        \"\"\"The cell (i, j) holding the point and the point's fractions inside it.\"\"\"\n        fx, fy = x / self.cell, y / self.cell\n        i = min(self.nx - 2, max(0, int(fx)))\n        j = min(self.ny - 2, max(0, int(fy)))\n        return i, j, fx - i, fy - j\n\n    def sample(self, x: float, y: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float, str]:\n        \"\"\"Height, d(height)/dx, d(height)/dy and terrain code at a point.\"\"\"\n        cell = self.cell\n        fx, fy = x / cell, y / cell\n        i = min(self.nx - 2, max(0, int(fx)))\n        j = min(self.ny - 2, max(0, int(fy)))\n        tx, ty = fx - i, fy - j\n        low, high = self.h[j], self.h[j + 1]\n        h00, h10, h01, h11 = low[i], low[i + 1], high[i], high[i + 1]\n        height = (h00 * (1 - tx) + h10 * tx) * (1 - ty) + (h01 * (1 - tx) + h11 * tx) * ty\n        gx = ((h10 - h00) * (1 - ty) + (h11 - h01) * ty) / cell\n        gy = ((h01 - h00) * (1 - tx) + (h11 - h10) * tx) / cell\n        return height, gx, gy, self.codes[j][i]\n\n    def elevation(self, x: float, y: float) -> float:\n        return self.sample(x, y)[0]\n\n    def slope(self, x: float, y: float) -> float:\n        _, gx, gy, _ = self.sample(x, y)\n        return math.hypot(gx, gy)\n\n    def terrain(self, x: float, y: float) -> str:\n        return TERRAIN_CODES[self.sample(x, y)[3]]\n\n    def cell_max_slope(self, i: int, j: int) -> float:\n        \"\"\"The steepest slope anywhere in cell (i, j). On a bilinear patch that is at a corner.\"\"\"\n        low, high, cell = self.h[j], self.h[j + 1], self.cell\n        h00, h10, h01, h11 = low[i], low[i + 1], high[i], high[i + 1]\n        south, north = (h10 - h00) / cell, (h11 - h01) / cell\n        west, east = (h01 - h00) / cell, (h11 - h10) / cell\n        return max(math.hypot(south, west), math.hypot(south, east),\n                   math.hypot(north, west), math.hypot(north, east))\n\n\ndef drive(surface: Surface, physics: Dict[str, Any], x: float, y: float, heading_deg: float, metres: float,\n          slip_base: Dict[str, float], noise: float = 0.0, battery: Optional[float] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"One drive command: `metres` of wheel travel at `heading_deg` from (x, y).\n\n    Per step of `segment_m` wheel metres, with the ground sampled where the step starts:\n      grade  = slope along the heading (rise over run), cross = slope to the left of it\n      slip   = clip(slip_base[terrain] + slip_grade_gain[terrain] * max(0, grade) + noise, 0, slip_max)\n      the rover moves segment * (1 - slip) along the heading and\n      segment * side_slip_gain[terrain] * cross to the right (downhill across the heading)\n      energy = segment * drive_cost_per_wheel_m[terrain] + climb_cost_per_m * max(0, height gained)\n    The step is refused, and the drive ends, if it would leave the map (`stop` = \"map_boundary\")\n    or end on ground steeper than `max_tilt` (`stop` = \"tilt\"). With a `battery`, the drive also\n    ends when the battery is spent (`stop` = \"battery\").\n\n    Returns the end position, wheel and ground metres, the energy used and `stop` (None if the\n    whole command ran).\n    \"\"\"\n    radians = math.radians(heading_deg)\n    ux, uy = math.cos(radians), math.sin(radians)\n    segment_full = physics[\"segment_m\"]\n    gain, side, cost = physics[\"slip_grade_gain\"], physics[\"side_slip_gain\"], physics[\"drive_cost_per_wheel_m\"]\n    climb, slip_max, max_tilt = physics[\"climb_cost_per_m\"], physics[\"slip_max\"], physics[\"max_tilt\"]\n    width, height = surface.width, surface.height\n    remaining = float(metres)\n    wheel = ground = energy = 0.0\n    stop = None\n    here, gx, gy, code = surface.sample(x, y)\n    while remaining > 1e-9:\n        segment = min(segment_full, remaining)\n        name = TERRAIN_CODES[code]\n        grade = gx * ux + gy * uy\n        cross = -gx * uy + gy * ux\n        slip = slip_base[name] + gain[name] * (grade if grade > 0 else 0.0) + noise\n        slip = 0.0 if slip < 0 else (slip_max if slip > slip_max else slip)\n        forward = segment * (1.0 - slip)\n        sideways = segment * side[name] * cross\n        next_x = x + ux * forward + uy * sideways\n        next_y = y + uy * forward - ux * sideways\n        if not (0.0 <= next_x <= width and 0.0 <= next_y <= height):\n            stop = \"map_boundary\"\n            break\n        there, next_gx, next_gy, next_code = surface.sample(next_x, next_y)\n        if math.hypot(next_gx, next_gy) > max_tilt:\n            stop = \"tilt\"\n            break\n        spent = segment * cost[name] + climb * (there - here if there > here else 0.0)\n        if battery is not None and spent >= battery - energy:\n            energy = battery\n            wheel += segment\n            ground += math.hypot(next_x - x, next_y - y)\n            x, y = next_x, next_y\n            stop = \"battery\"\n            break\n        energy += spent\n        wheel += segment\n        ground += math.hypot(next_x - x, next_y - y)\n        remaining -= segment\n        x, y, here, gx, gy, code = next_x, next_y, there, next_gx, next_gy, next_code\n    return {\"x\": x, \"y\": y, \"wheel\": wheel, \"ground\": ground, \"energy\": energy, \"stop\": stop}\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Start a long-running program so that it outlives the shell command that started it.\n\n    python3 /app/detach.py python3 autopilot.py                  # output goes to ./autopilot.log\n    python3 /app/detach.py --log second.log python3 autopilot.py\n\nPrints the process id and returns at once. Stop the program with `kill <pid>`.\n\nWhy this exists. An agent's shell tool runs one command at a time under a time limit. Such a\ntool typically waits until everything the command started has let go of its output, and when\nthe limit is reached it stops the whole process group. A program started with `&` or `nohup`\nis still in that group, and in a form like `cd /app && nohup python3 autopilot.py > log 2>&1 &`\nthe shell that waits for it still holds the tool's output. The call then hangs until the limit\nand the program is killed with it, in the middle of a campaign that does not wait.\n\nA program started here has its own session and no link to the caller's input or output: it\nreads from nowhere and writes to the log file, unbuffered so the log is current. Standard\nlibrary only; needs a POSIX system.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom typing import Optional, Sequence\n\n\ndef start(command: Sequence[str], log: str = \"autopilot.log\") -> int:\n    \"\"\"Start `command` detached, appending its output to `log`; return its process id.\"\"\"\n    environment = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=\"1\")\n    with open(log, \"ab\") as stream:\n        process = subprocess.Popen(list(command), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=stream,\n                                   stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True,\n                                   close_fds=True, env=environment)\n    return process.pid\n\n\ndef main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Start a program that keeps running after this command returns.\",\n        usage=\"python3 detach.py [--log FILE] command [argument ...]\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--log\", default=\"autopilot.log\", help=\"file the program's output is appended to\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"command\", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, help=\"the program and its arguments\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    command = args.command[1:] if args.command[:1] == [\"--\"] else args.command\n    if not command:\n        parser.error(\"give the program to start, for example: python3 autopilot.py\")\n    try:\n        pid = start(command, args.log)\n    except OSError as failure:\n        print(\"could not start {}: {}\".format(command[0], failure), file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    print(\"started pid {}; its output goes to {}; stop it with: kill {}\".format(\n        pid, os.path.abspath(args.log), pid))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"Play a Lightlag MCP server from ordinary, synchronous Python.\n\n`connect(target)` yields an object with the five public methods, each making a\nreal MCP tool call. Scripted controllers can therefore run through the same\nservice a model would use:\n\n    from lightlag_controllers import REFERENCE, drive, make\n    from lightlag_mcp.client import connect\n\n    with connect(\"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp\") as tools:\n        drive(tools, make(REFERENCE))\n\n`target` is a URL (Streamable HTTP), `StdioServerParameters`, or a server object\nfor in-process tests. Requires the `mcp` package, version 2.x.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport asyncio\nimport concurrent.futures\nimport contextlib\nimport json\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List\n\nfrom mcp import Client\n\n\nclass RemoteToolError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The server rejected a call. A ValueError, like the simulator's own rejections.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass McpTools:\n    \"\"\"The five public methods, each a blocking MCP tool call.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, client: Client, loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop) -> None:\n        self._client = client\n        self._loop = loop\n\n    def _call(self, tool: str, arguments: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(self._client.call_tool(tool, arguments), self._loop)\n        result = future.result()\n        text = \"\".join(getattr(block, \"text\", \"\") for block in result.content)\n        if result.is_error:\n            raise RemoteToolError(text)\n        return json.loads(text)\n\n    def rules(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        return self._call(\"rules\", {})\n\n    def map(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        return self._call(\"map\", {})\n\n    def telemetry_log(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n        return self._call(\"telemetry_log\", {})\n\n    def uplink(self, commands: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n        return self._call(\"uplink\", {\"commands\": commands})\n\n    def advance(self, ticks: int = 1) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        return self._call(\"advance\", {\"ticks\": ticks})\n\n    def tool_names(self) -> List[str]:\n        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(self._client.list_tools(), self._loop)\n        return [tool.name for tool in future.result().tools]\n\n\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef connect(target: Any) -> Iterator[McpTools]:\n    \"\"\"Open an MCP session on a background event loop and yield blocking tools.\"\"\"\n    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()\n    thread = threading.Thread(target=loop.run_forever, name=\"lightlag-mcp-client\", daemon=True)\n    thread.start()\n    ready: \"concurrent.futures.Future[Client]\" = concurrent.futures.Future()\n    stop_holder: List[asyncio.Event] = []\n\n    async def session() -> None:\n        # The session is opened and closed inside one task, as the SDK requires.\n        stop = asyncio.Event()\n        stop_holder.append(stop)\n        try:\n            async with Client(target) as client:\n                ready.set_result(client)\n                await stop.wait()\n        except BaseException as failure:\n            if not ready.done():\n                ready.set_exception(failure)\n                return\n            raise\n\n    running = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(session(), loop)\n    try:\n        client = ready.result(timeout=30)\n        try:\n            yield McpTools(client, loop)\n        finally:\n            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(stop_holder[0].set)\n            running.result(timeout=30)\n    finally:\n        loop.call_soon_threadsafe(loop.stop)\n        thread.join(timeout=5)\n        loop.close()\n","metadata":{"output":"total 24\ndrwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 14 15:03 .\ndrwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Nov 14 18:58 ..\n-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2830 Nov 14 15:03 detach.py\n-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 3518 Nov 14 11:06 lightlag_client.py\n-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 7822 Nov 14 15:03 lightlag_surface.py\n  102 lightlag_client.py\n  152 lightlag_surface.py\n   61 detach.py\n  315 total\n\"\"\"The ground and the drive physics of the traverse, as published.\n\nEverything here is public: `rules()` gives the numbers and `map()` the grid. applied.\nStandard library only, Python 3.9+.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple\n\nTERRAIN_CODES = {\"b\": \"sand\": 3.5, \"rocks\": 1.2},\n    \"slip_noise\": 0.02,                 # one uniform draw in +-this per executed drive\n    \"slip_max\": 0.95,\n    \"side_slip_gain\": {\"bedrock\": 0.1, \"regolith\": 0.3, \"sand\": 0.8, \"rocks\": 0.2},\n    \"drive_cost_per_wheel_m\": {\"bedrock\": 0.30, \"regolith\": 0.36, \"sand\": 0.50, \"rocks\": 0.60},\n    \"climb_cost_per_m\": 2.0,            # energy per metre of height gained; descending returns nothing\n}\n\n\nclass Surface:\n    \"\"\"A height grid with bilinear interpolation, and one terrain class per grid cell.\n\n    `elevation_cm[j][i]` is the height in centimetres at x = i * cell, y = j * cell.\n    `terrain[j][i]` is the class code of the cell with that vertex as its south-west corner.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, cell: float, elevation_cm: Sequence[Sequence[int]], terrain: Sequence[str]) -> None:\n        self.cell = float(cell)\n        self.h: List[List[float]] = [[value / 100.0 for value in row] for row in elevation_cm]\n        self.ny, self.nx = len(self.h), len(self.h[0])\n        if self.ny < 2 or self.nx < 2 or any(len(row) != self.nx for row in self.h):\n            raise ValueError(\"the elevation grid must be rectangular, at least 2 by 2\")\n        if len(terrain) != self.ny - 1 or any(len(row) != self.nx - 1 for row in terrain):\n            raise ValueError(\"terrain needs one code per grid cell\")\n        self.codes: List[str] = [str(row) for row in terrain]\n        self.width = (self.nx - 1) * self.cell\n        self.height = (self.ny - 1) * self.cell\n\n    def inside(self, x: float, y: float) -> bool:\n        return 0.0 <= x <= self.width and 0.0 <= y <= self.height\n\n    def locate(self, x: float, y: float) -> Tuple[int, int, float, float]:\n        \"\"\"The cell (i, j) holding the point and the point's fractions inside it.\"\"\"\n        fx, fy = x / self.cell, y / self.cell\n        i = min(self.nx - 2, max(0, int(fx)))\n        j = min(self.ny - 2, max(0, int(fy)))\n        return i, j, fx - i, fy - j\n\n    def sample(self, x: float, y: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float, str]:\n        \"\"\"Height, d(height)/dx, d(height)/dy and terrain code at a point.\"\"\"\n        cell = self.cell\n        fx, fy = x / cell, y / cell\n        i = min(self.nx - 2, max(0, int(fx)))\n        j = min(self.ny - 2, max(0, int(fy)))\n        tx, ty = fx - i, fy - j\n        low, high = self.h[j], self.h[j + 1]\n        h00, h10, h01, h11 = low[i], low[i + 1], high[i], high[i + 1]\n        height = (h00 * (1 - tx) + h10 * tx) * (1 - ty) + (h01 * (1 - tx) + h11 * tx) * ty\n        gx = ((h10 - h00) * (1 - ty) + (h11 - h01) * ty) / cell\n        gy = ((h01 - h00) * (1 - tx) + (h11 - h10) * tx) / cell\n        return height, gx, gy, self.codes[j][i]\n\n    def elevation(self, x: float, y: float) -> float:\n        return self.sample(x, y)[0]\n\n    def slope(self, x: float, y: float) -> float:\n        _, gx, gy, _ = self.sample(x, y)\n        return math.hypot(gx, gy)\n\n    def terrain(self, x: float, y: float) -> str:\n        return TERRAIN_CODES[self.sample(x, y)[3]]\n\n    def cell_max_slope(self, i: int, j: int) -> float:\n        \"\"\"The steepest slope anywhere in cell (i, j). On a bilinear patch that is at a corner.\"\"\"\n        low, high, cell = self.h[j], self.h[j + 1], self.cell\n        h00, h10, h01, h11 = low[i], low[i + 1], high[i], high[i + 1]\n        south, north = (h10 - h00) / cell, (h11 - h01) / cell\n        west, east = (h01 - h00) / cell, (h11 - h10) / cell\n        return max(math.hypot(south, west), math.hypot(south, east),\n                   math.hypot(north, west), math.hypot(north, east))\n\n\ndef drive(surface: Surface, physics: Dict[str, Any], x: float, y: float, heading_deg: float, metres: float,\n          slip_base: Dict[str, float], noise: float = 0.0, battery: Optional[float] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"One drive command: `metres` of wheel travel at `heading_deg` from (x, y).\n\n    Per step of `segment_m` wheel metres, with the ground sampled where the step starts:\n      grade  = slope along the heading (rise over run), cross = slope to the left of it\n      slip   = clip(slip_base[terrain] + slip_grade_gain[terrain] * max(0, grade) + noise, 0, slip_max)\n      the rover moves segment * (1 - slip) along the heading and\n      segment * side_slip_gain[terrain] * cross to the right (downhill across the heading)\n      energy = segment * drive_cost_per_wheel_m[terrain] + climb_cost_per_m * max(0, height gained)\n    The step is refused, and the drive ends, if it would leave the map (`stop` = \"map_boundary\")\n    or end on ground steeper than `max_tilt` (`stop` = \"tilt\"). With a `battery`, the drive also\n    ends when the battery is spent (`stop` = \"battery\").\n\n    Returns the end position, wheel and ground metres, the energy used and `stop` (None if the\n    whole command ran).\n    \"\"\"\n    radians = math.radians(heading_deg)\n    ux, uy = math.cos(radians), math.sin(radians)\n    segment_full = physics[\"segment_m\"]\n    gain, side, cost = physics[\"slip_grade_gain\"], physics[\"side_slip_gain\"], physics[\"drive_cost_per_wheel_m\"]\n    climb, slip_max, max_tilt = physics[\"climb_cost_per_m\"], physics[\"slip_max\"], physics[\"max_tilt\"]\n    width, height = surface.width, surface.height\n    remaining = float(metres)\n    wheel = ground = energy = 0.0\n    stop = None\n    here, gx, gy, code = surface.sample(x, y)\n    while remaining > 1e-9:\n        segment = min(segment_full, remaining)\n        name = TERRAIN_CODES[code]\n        grade = gx * ux + gy * uy\n        cross = -gx * uy + gy * ux\n        slip = slip_base[name] + gain[name] * (grade if grade > 0 else 0.0) + noise\n        slip = 0.0 if slip < 0 else (slip_max if slip > slip_max else slip)\n        forward = segment * (1.0 - slip)\n        sideways = segment * side[name] * cross\n        next_x = x + ux * forward + uy * sideways\n        next_y = y + uy * forward - ux * sideways\n        if not (0.0 <= next_x <= width and 0.0 <= next_y <= height):\n            stop = \"map_boundary\"\n            break\n        there, next_gx, next_gy, next_code = surface.sample(next_x, next_y)\n        if math.hypot(next_gx, next_gy) > max_tilt:\n            stop = \"tilt\"\n            break\n        spent = segment * cost[name] + climb * (there - here if there > here else 0.0)\n        if battery is not None and spent >= battery - energy:\n            energy = battery\n            wheel += segment\n            ground += math.hypot(next_x - x, next_y - y)\n            x, y = next_x, next_y\n            stop = \"battery\"\n            break\n        energy += spent\n        wheel += segment\n        ground += math.hypot(next_x - x, next_y - y)\n        remaining -= segment\n        x, y, here, gx, gy, code = next_x, next_y, there, next_gx, next_gy, next_code\n    return {\"x\": x, \"y\": y, \"wheel\": wheel, \"ground\": ground, \"energy\": energy, \"stop\": stop}\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Start a long-running program so that it outlives the shell command that started it.\n\n    python3 /app/detach.py python3 autopilot.py                  # output goes to ./autopilot.log\n    python3 /app/detach.py --log second.log python3 autopilot.py\n\nPrints the process id and returns at once. Stop the program with `kill <pid>`.\n\nWhy this exists. An agent's shell tool runs one command at a time under a time limit. Such a\ntool typically waits until everything the command started has let go of its output, and when\nthe limit is reached it stops the whole process group. A program started with `&` or `nohup`\nis still in that group, and in a form like `cd /app && nohup python3 autopilot.py > log 2>&1 &`\nthe shell that waits for it still holds the tool's output. The call then hangs until the limit\nand the program is killed with it, in the middle of a campaign that does not wait.\n\nA program started here has its own session and no link to the caller's input or output: it\nreads from nowhere and writes to the log file, unbuffered so the log is current. Standard\nlibrary only; needs a POSIX system.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom typing import Optional, Sequence\n\n\ndef start(command: Sequence[str], log: str = \"autopilot.log\") -> int:\n    \"\"\"Start `command` detached, appending its output to `log`; return its process id.\"\"\"\n    environment = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=\"1\")\n    with open(log, \"ab\") as stream:\n        process = subprocess.Popen(list(command), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=stream,\n                                   stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True,\n                                   close_fds=True, env=environment)\n    return process.pid\n\n\ndef main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Start a program that keeps running after this command returns.\",\n        usage=\"python3 detach.py [--log FILE] command [argument ...]\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--log\", default=\"autopilot.log\", help=\"file the program's output is appended to\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"command\", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, help=\"the program and its arguments\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    command = args.command[1:] if args.command[:1] == [\"--\"] else args.command\n    if not command:\n        parser.error(\"give the program to start, for example: python3 autopilot.py\")\n    try:\n        pid = start(command, args.log)\n    except OSError as failure:\n        print(\"could not start {}: {}\".format(command[0], failure), file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    print(\"started pid {}; its output goes to {}; stop it with: kill {}\".format(\n        pid, os.path.abspath(args.log), pid))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"Play a Lightlag MCP server from ordinary, synchronous Python.\n\n`connect(target)` yields an object with the five public methods, each making a\nreal MCP tool call.
